title: Automated escrow + quarantine flow for encumbered model artifacts
creator: Hannah Park
description: Background: During model ingestion we frequently encounter artifacts whose license metadata or weight provenance is ambiguous (partial license text, missing manifest, or third-party encoder blobs). Current onboarding gates either block ingestion entirely or require ad-hoc manual review, which creates friction for customers and delays model availability. Scope: Implement a dual-path compliance flow that (1) applies deterministic heuristics to surface likely-encumbered models, (2) places flagged artifacts into a short-lived "quarantine" state with constrained serving policy, and (3) offers an automated escrow and attestation path that allows temporary restricted-serving for evaluation while legal/ops resolve provenance. Goals: reduce manual review load by >=60% for common license mismatches, provide safe temporary evaluation access with clear audit trail, and ensure enforcement hooks (auto-block, rollback) are available to runtime teams. Out of scope: changes to public pricing or long-term escrow custody (handled by Legal).
acceptance_criteria: Quarantine state implemented in onboarding API: ingest returns status 'quarantined' and reason codes
Heuristics engine implemented and documented: license token-matching, manifest parity check, signature provenance scoring
Limited-serving policy for quarantined models: max 10 QPS, read-only logs, watermarking of outputs, and traceable request headers
Escrow automation: when submitter opts-in, artifacts are uploaded to escrow bucket with TTL and attestation form link generated
Operational dashboards: queue length, avg manual reviews avoided, latency impact, security audit log
Rollback path: runtime automatically disables restricted-serving if legal rejects within TTL
Documentation: PRD, runbook for legal/ops, and developer quickstart with sample cURLs
